# Contracts audit and schema-twin reuse

Read-only audit on codex/world-aware-tools at 527cdd0bc. Package source matched main at the start of the audit. Audit captured before product changes; canonical-schema reuse now tracked in #2512.

## Scope and measured results

- Structural inventory: 130 files, 31,431 TypeScript lines; preset/index.ts alone has 3,368 lines. Size describes concentration, not proof of dead code.
- Native AST testonly: 39 Contracts candidates (18 schemas, 7 type aliases, 5 functions, 9 constants/maps).
- Native AST orphans: 29 reportable candidates, plus 5 conservatively suppressed by star re-exports. Scan completed over 129 source files. These are candidate counts, not deletion counts.
- Enum constructor census: 86 exported Contracts z.enum schema declarations; 282 z.enum calls across package TypeScript. Name matches generated candidates; source imports/intent must disambiguate origins. This is not an exhaustive audit of every possible Zod object/refinement or dynamic validator.

Full combined `rot contracts` completed successfully: 29 orphans, 39 test-only, zero dead chains, 2 type-only schemas, zero swallowed results. It scanned 129 Contracts source files with repository-wide reference coverage, took 11:01.51, and peaked at 14,674,376 KiB RSS. All sections reported complete. The two type-only results are characterBulkTagResultSchema and imageCaptionMetaSchema; both govern live inferred types. characterBulkTagResultSchema would require adding new RPC output validation, not replacing a duplicate. imageCaptionMetaSchema describes persisted metadata, while the producer already validates imageBreakdownSchema; inserting the persisted schema into legacy reads would reject null fields that current defensive readers deliberately tolerate. Neither is part of the reuse patch.

## Confirmed RPG twin reuse opportunities

Fifteen production constructors rebuild twelve existing schema twins from the same canonical tuples. All twelve existing schema parsers matched freshly constructed enum parsers for every tuple member and seven invalid-input shapes (129 comparisons). Keep wrappers/defaults/descriptions at each call site. Reuse the existing schemas; do not delete the twins.

## Other checked candidates

- Discovery: `duplicateRelationSchema` versus discovery router line57; use the schema with the existing `.optional()` wrapper.
- Settings: `memoryRetrievalModeSchema` versus settings/index.ts101; retain `.optional().describe(...)`.
- Environment: `authModeSchema` versus foundation/env/index.ts411; same enum with existing default; keep separate from changes to authentication semantics.
- Automation: globalVariableKeySchema versus manual min/max length checks in set-global-variable.ts14-18; shared predicate is possible, preserving domain-specific errors.
- ConnectionRef: strict connection TypeID schema versus transport brandedId nonempty-string schema. This is a behavior change, not an equivalent substitution; focused security review confirms a low-severity validation-contract defect. All 12 procedures retain owner-scoped lookup before effects; no authorization bypass found. Reuse the canonical connectionId property, retain nullable binding clearing, and prove malformed/wrong-kind rejection before service dispatch. Supported production and seed paths mint the proper TypeID; manually inserted malformed rows are the compatibility caveat.

## Intentionally distinct / reserved

- Preset effort vocabulary includes `none`; model effort vocabulary does not. Equal identifier spellings are not equal axes.
- Kit injection cannot import Contracts messageRoleSchema upward. Package direction wins over superficial deduplication.
- Automation outcome storage adds `reserved`; delta persistence is narrower than all wire delta kinds.
- Rule-preset scope and automation-variable scope are explicitly separate axes despite equal string members.
- Normalized finish reasons are produced by a raw-to-normalized mapping; DB derives its enum directly from the tuple.
- Clip kind/source/scope schema twins are explicitly reserved v2 vocabulary. No artificial runtime reader is warranted.

## Runtime helper findings requiring intent review

- foldActiveSpace: tests retain an older space-fold model; production search persistence now uses active/candidate generation IDs and different states.
- evidenceRank: tested evidence ordering is documented as canonical, while synthesis spells ordering separately in three folds.
- CONTENT_CLASS_POLICY: deliberate test oracle/totality table, with stale wording claiming direct production reading.
- MODE_POLICY: reserved future mode data; comments describe a capability reader absent from the current tree.
- taskProviders and resolveTrackerCarriers: test-only inverse queries around live sibling operations.

No bulk deletion or package redesign follows from this audit. Reuse proven-equivalent schema twins first; adjudicate behavior changes and stale contract claims separately.
